citations.quote: The INVALID clause takes effect during the relation validation stage of the execution of a VALIDATE statement.
The INVALID clause takes effect during the relation validation stage of the execution of a VALIDATE statement.
The INVALID clause feature of the VALIDATE facility is an obsolete feature.
An implementation may optionally provide the elements specified in Annex A, Communications facility.
An implementation shall accept the syntax and provide the functionality for all standard language elements required by this International Standard

cases.reason: The words, format (INVALID WHEN condition-1) and the VALIDATE stages are the same. But the 2023 row is a non-support verdict licensed by 2023 Annex A.4.14, and 2002 licenses no such decline: §2002:3.1 says a conforming implementation shall provide the normative elements of clauses 6 to 16 and may optionally provide only Annex A (communications), and §2002:3.1.1 requires it to accept the syntax and provide the functionality of every required element. VALIDATE (14.8.46) and the INVALID clause (13.16.29) are in clauses 13 and 14 and are not in B.3. The compiler refuses the clause at --std 2002, so the 2002 rule has no evidence and the observed behaviour contradicts the 2002 text.

the relation validation stage of a VALIDATE statement whose operand is or contains the entry

cases.needs: 2002 requires the VALIDATE facility (the INVALID clause and the VALIDATE statement's relation validation stage); the compiler declines it
cases.compiler-at-2002: wrong: validate-invalid.cob at --std 2002 exits 65: warning COBOL1580 'The VALIDATE facility (ISO §2023:14.9.50) is an OPTIONAL element (§2023:4.2.7; Annex A.4.14) ... not supported', then error COBOL1708 refusing the INVALID WHEN clause. Expected under §2002:3.1 and §2002:3.1.1: the program compiles and runs, printing 'AFTER VALIDATE A=0000' and 'AFTER VALIDATE A=0005'. In the first VALIDATE, WS-A = 0 makes condition-1 true, the internal indicator is set to invalid on relation, and EC-VALIDATE and EC-VALIDATE-RELATION are set to exist (non-fatal, unchecked by default, §2002:14.8.46.3 GR6). Same output at --std 2023, where the decline is licensed.
flags-answered: target-not-CONFORMS-OK: the 2023 twin is DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT under 2023 Annex A.4.14 (VALIDATE optional; also obsolete in 2023, 13.18.31.1 NOTE). 2002 has no such licence. 3.1 makes only Annex A (the communications facility) optional. VALIDATE is not in B.3, the processor-dependent list, and it is not obsolete in 2002. So the 2002 rule requires the feature, and the decline at --std 2002 rejects legal 2002 source.
